layout_dets.text: Role of Nitrogen in the Pitting Resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of Cast Duplex CF-Type Stainless Steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: S. J. Pawel,* E. E. Stansbury,** and C. D. Lundin**

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this investigation, critical manipulation, observation, and analy-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sis of polarization curves as a function of nitrogen content in cast

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duplex CF-type stainless steels (SSs) has been performed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These, in conjunction with microstructural observations and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: atomic absorption spectroscopic analyses of polarization cell so-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lutions, have led to the discovery of nitrogen's major role in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance of SSs. Nitrogen has been found to encour-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: age the retention of chromium in the passive film and near sur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: face layers during corrosion, which improves pitting resistance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: During the past 10 to 15 years, nitrogen has become an important

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy addition to many wrought austenitic stainless steels (SSs).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Initially, nitrogen was added as a less costly austenite former than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nickel. An additional motivation for adding nitrogen to SSs results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the increased use of low-carbon grades of wrought austenitic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SSs in power generation applications, particularly in boiling water

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reactor (BWR) and pressurized water reactor (PWR) plant piping.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The use of low-carbon alloys is necessitated by the need to avoid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: welding related corrosion problems (i.e., sensitization). Nitrogen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has become a common alloying addition to return the strength of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low-carbon alloys to that of nominal carbon content alloys. During

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this material development period, data have accumulated on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects of nitrogen additions on corrosion properties of wrought

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SSs, strongly suggesting that nitrogen improves intergranular and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion resistance in these steels.1.2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The high-alloy casting industry is adding nitrogen to selected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grades of corrosion-resistant castings in response to the demand

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for higher performance alloys and as a consequence of the suc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cess the wrought alloy industry has had with nitrogen additions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Unfortunately, there is a small amount of data on nitrogen effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the corrosion behavior of high-alloy duplex cast materials. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: response, research was initiated to document the magnitude of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvement in localized corrosion resistance resulting from nitro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gen additions in cast duplex SSs and to elucidate the mechanism

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by which this improvement occurs. This paper describes some of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the results regarding the pitting resistance of solution treated CF-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: type alloys. CF-type alloys are the cast equivalent of AISI(1)304

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SSs; the major difference is that CF alloys generally contain 5 to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 25% ferrite in the microstructure, while AISI 304 SS is nominally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fully austenitic.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alloys and Preparation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Because of the complex interrelationships between ferrite-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and austenite-forming elements in duplex SSs (see, for example

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Schoefer diagram),³ it is impossible to vary the concentration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of only one component and maintain a constant ferrite content.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, within the range of nickel concentrations commonly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found in the alloys of interest, nickel does not appear to be a par-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ticularly important variable in the localized corrosion resistance of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SSs.2,4 Therefore, it was decided to “isolate" nitrogen as a com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: positional variable by making alloys with fixed Cr, Mo, and C con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tents and decreasing the nickel content as the amount of nitrogen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is increased to maintain approximately constant ferrite.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A base melting stock for CF-type alloys was prepared and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cast into cylindrical shapes of a size convenient for remelting in a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Balzers(²) induction furnace. High-purity Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, and graph-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ite powders were used to adjust the composition of the base stock

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the desired values. This technique enabled careful composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: control and alloys of identical residual elemental content to be pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duced. High-nitrogen ferrochrome facilitated the addition of nitro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gen to each melt.The compositions (based on chemical analysis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: following casting) of the alloys produced in this manner (labeled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CF-11 through -14) and two similar alloys (labeled CF-3 and -4)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: studied in this investigation are given in Table 1.The range of fer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rite contents (7 to 15 as measured by a magne-gage) for the al-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loys produced by the authors (CF-11 through -14) is a result of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inability to precisely predict the efficiency of nitrogen transfer from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the ferrochrome to the melt. Based on the results from many test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: castings, the nitrogen transfer efficiency varies between ~70 and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 90%. Alloys CF-13 and -14 were analyzed following casting and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were found to contain less nitrogen than the target value; if the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intended nitrogen level had been achieved, it is likely that the fer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rite content would have fallen in the target range of 6 to 9 (magne-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gage).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The test begins at the open circuit potential (Ec). Once a stable

layout_dets.text: active

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the polarization scan was reversed was chosen to represent a

layout_dets.text: compromise between a value large enough to ensure the onset of

layout_dets.text: stable pitting and one small enough to enable microstructural de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: During this investigation, it was found that special precautions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were necessary to ensure that crevice corrosion at the edges of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the sample mount did not occur. Therefore, samples for polariza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion (Figure 2) were prepassivated in 50% nitric acid (50 C) follow-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing polishing through 9-μm diamond paste. The edges of the sam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ple were then painted with a tough corrosion-resistant enamel.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Immediately before testing, a cotton swab with diamond paste was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used to remove the passive film from the exposed portion of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sample, leaving the passive film under the protective enamel at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the sample edges. This technique has been shown⁵ to eliminate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spurious crevices that form at sample mount edges or at the ena-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mel/sample interface (the latter frequently occurring if the prepas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sivation step is omitted); otherwise, data interpretation is compli-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cated in at least two ways. Typically, crevice corrosion occurs at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: much lower potentials than pitting corrosion. If çrevice-type corro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion is misinterpreted as pitting corrosion for some alloys or sam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ples and not for others, similar phenomena are not being com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pared if these mixed corrosion values are used to rank the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: localized corrosion resistance. In addition, crevices often lead to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gradual current increases (from the passive CD) rather than the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: normal sharp current increase that determines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in a standard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cyclic polarization test. By using the enamel masking technique,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the relative pitting potentials of the exposed sample surfaces may

layout_dets.text: Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The analysis of a polarization curve yields information such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as the relative ability of an alloy to passivate or its susceptibility to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion. The CD value that is determined at any potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: represents the net current at the sample surface and no informa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion concerning the ionic composition of this current is available

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the polarization curve. To obtain information on the distribu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of ionic species responsible for the anodic current, chemical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analysis of the test solution following a polarization experiment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: must be performed. In this investigation, chemical analyses of test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions were performed using atomic absorption spectrometry

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (AAS). A Perkin-Elmer(³) Zeeman/3030 system, comprising spec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trometer, Zeeman graphite furnace unit, and auto-sampler, was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used for all AAS determinations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Samples were potentiostatically etched in the pitting test solu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion at potentials near that of the maximum anodic dissolution CD

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and at a potential just greater than that necessary to induce pas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . During dissolution, the CD as a function of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time was recorded so that the total amount of charge transferred

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: could be calculated. The concentration of each of the major alloy-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing elements (Fe, Cr, Ni, and Mo) in each test solution, normalized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to unit charge transferred, was then determined and related to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bulk composition of the alloy in question.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Determination of the contribution of the major alloying ele-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments to the dissolution current yields important information about

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the dissolution process as a function of alloy content, but it also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indirectly yields information about the surface (passive film and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: near-surface bulk alloy) composition of the alloy. For example,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other factors such as dissolution potential and test environment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: being equal, a test solution that is determined to have a very low

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromium concentration (compared to that following testing of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different alloy) indicates that the corresponding alloy must have a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surface relatively rich in chromium. This follows because the chro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mium must be located in the alloy (unoxidized state), in the pas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sive film (oxidized state), or in the test solution. Such information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may be used in much the same way (qualitatively) as information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: obtained from surface analysis techniques.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In view of the preceding discussion, it seems plausible to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: known by what mechanism this occurs. It can be speculated that,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: because of the known affinity of chromium for nitrogen, the fact

layout_dets.text: that nitrogen slows chromium diffusion in the austenite16,17 and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that nitrogen accumulates at the metal/oxide interface during

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion,18 chromium is retained in the passive film (and near

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surface layers) because of a chromium/nitrogen interaction (similar

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to a clustering effect), which inhibits both diffusion and dissolution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: CONCLUSIONS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The present research, through critical manipulation, observa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion, and analysis of cyclic polarization curves as a function of ni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mined by cyclic polarization procedure modified such that no NaCi

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trogen content of the CF alloys, has led to a description of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanism of the improvement in pitting resistance resulting from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen additions. It is hypothesized that the change in shape and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: position of the anodic loop as a function of nitrogen content results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from contributions from two dissolution processes that occur in a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: magnitude related to the amount of nitrogen in austenite. Specifi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cally, for high-nitrogen contents, the anodic loop of the cyclic po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: larization curve splits into two active loops. The high potential loop

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was found to be common to all alloys of this general composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: class, but the low potential loop increased in magnitude and oc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curred at lower potentials as the nitrogen content increased. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observation that this low potential loop closely resembles the po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: larization curve for the active dissolution of iron in similar solutions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: suggests that nitrogen encourages the dissolution of iron and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accumulation of chromium during the initial stages of active disso-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The pitting of high-nitrogen alloys was observed to be very

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sensitive to procedure variations designed to vary the influence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the active dissolution processes occurring on passing through the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low potential loop (i.e., during the early stages of active dissolu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion). The pitting test results for the low-nitrogen alloys were not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: influenced by these procedure variations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It was also shown, with atomic absorption spectroscopy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (AAS), that increasing nitrogen in CF alloys decreases the amount

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of chromium found in solution following potentiostatic dissolution at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a variety of potentials. Since the chromium content of the solution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is lower with increasing nitrogen content of the alloy, chromium

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: must be accumulating at the surface (in the passive film or near

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surface layers) of the nitrogen-containing alloys. Thus, in the pres-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ence of solid solution nitrogen, the surface chromium content of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the alloy is effectively increased and the pitting resistance is ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: served to improve. The observed trend of the nitrogen effect on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromium accumulation was observed at al dissolution potentials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: examined, but this effect was greatest for active dissolution at po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tentials near that of the low potential loop.

layout_dets.text: Finally, it is proposed that, on an atomic scale, the affinity of

layout_dets.text: other observations noted in the literature, such as the facts that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
